procedure.description: panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 15847 (panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen) with date of service 2026-08-18. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: The documentation does not establish a functional impairment or failure of conservative treatment of the skin condition.

criteria.text: Panniculus hangs at or below the level of the pubis (grade 2 or higher) as documented on examination.

Recurrent or chronic intertrigo, cellulitis, or skin breakdown beneath the panniculus that has failed at least 3 months of conservative treatment such as topical antifungals, hygiene measures, and barrier products.
Weight stable within 10 pounds for at least 6 months.
The panniculus interferes with activities of daily living or ambulation.

chart.text: Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

36 year old woman here about the abdominal apron after her weight loss. Nice result on the weight. Discussed panniculectomy versus a full abdominoplasty and what insurance will and will not look at. Her history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor, reflux on omeprazole as needed, migraines, rare now. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives with her spouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. On exam the pannus hangs well below the pubis, I would call it grade 2, with maceration and an odor in the fold. Down 118 pounds after the sleeve in 2023. Weight has been steady at 182 give or take five for the last 15 months. Says she cannot walk more than a block without the skin fold chafing raw, has to lift it to wash underneath, cannot find pants that fit over it.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.4, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 50. Repeat in a year.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.

Follow-up on the abdomen. Went back over the operation, drains, the scar, recovery of four to six weeks. She understands this is skin and fat removal for the skin problems, not a tummy tuck. Vitals today 125 over 89, pulse 69. Weight 183 today, holding.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 229, LDL 127, HDL 38, triglycerides 170. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Vitamin D came back 14. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Blood pressure check. 140 over 78 today, 126 over 74 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. She asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 4 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Pre-op. Consent signed. Marked the resection with her standing. Nicotine negative. Hold the metformin the morning of.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-2 (skin); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
